blurb: Compact tuxedo-marked American dog nicknamed the American Gentleman
description: The Boston Terrier is a small, compact dog from the US with a short muzzle, erect ears and tuxedo-like markings, described as friendly and easy to train.
answer: The Boston Terrier is a small, compact breed that originated in Boston, Massachusetts, around 1870 and was accepted by the AKC in 1893. It weighs up to about 11 kg, has a short muzzle, erect ears and white tuxedo markings, and is described as eager to please and sociable.

body: The breed traces to Hooper's Judge, a bull-and-terrier type dog bought in Boston around 1870, which the AKC cites as the ancestor of nearly all modern Boston Terriers. Judge was bred to a white bulldog-type female, and later breeders reduced the size of the early Old Boston Bulldogs.

The Boston Terrier Club formed in 1891 and joined the AKC in 1893, making this one of the few breeds developed in the United States. It has been the state dog of Massachusetts since 1979, and Sergeant Stubby, a celebrated First World War dog, is often described as a Boston Bull Terrier.

The Boston is compact and well proportioned, with a square head, erect ears, a short wrinkle-free muzzle, a broad chest and a naturally short tail. International standards set a maximum of 11 kg, and the AKC shows it in three weight classes. The coat is black, brindle or seal with white on the chest, muzzle and between the eyes; large, round, widely set eyes are a hallmark.

Boston Terriers are generally described as eager to please and easily trained, quiet, barking mainly when necessary, and fond of people. When properly socialized they are said to get along with children, older people, other dogs and other pets, though some males may challenge other dogs.

Their quiet nature is often said to suit apartment life. As a short-muzzled breed they can struggle to cool down by panting, so owners are commonly advised to avoid overheating; sources give little other care detail.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.8 years. As a brachycephalic breed, conditions reported include brachycephalic airway obstructive syndrome, overheating, skin fold dermatitis and anesthetic risks. Others include hereditary cataracts, atopic dermatitis, demodicosis and mast cell tumours, and over 80% of litters in one UK survey were delivered by caesarean section.

faq.q: How big does a Boston Terrier get?
faq.a: International standards set a maximum weight of about 11 kg, and the AKC divides the breed into classes under 15 lb, 15 to under 20 lb, and 20 to 25 lb.

faq.q: Are Boston Terriers good with children?
faq.a: When properly socialized they are generally described as getting along well with children, older people and other pets.

faq.q: How long do Boston Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11.8 years for the breed.
